facts.text: Sweet Grass is a port of entry near the Canadian border, sharing a joint facility with Coutts, Alberta that opened in 2004.
The town’s name comes from the sweetgrass plant, sacred to Indigenous peoples and once common along the river bottoms.
Sweet Grass County sits between the Yellowstone River and the Crazy Mountains, offering a dramatic shift from river bottomlands to alpine terrain in under an hour.
The Crazy Mountain Museum on Second Avenue East showcases the area’s Crow heritage, early settler history, and ranching legacy in a modest building.
The Boulder River corridor is a fly‑fishing and camping paradise, drawing anglers to brown and rainbow trout from May onward.
Sweet Grass is the northern terminus of Interstate 15, a key link connecting western Canada, the western United States, and Mexico.
